monologue: The card hums warm at forty-eight, making every flat edge feel too thin to hold the turnip. I am awake in the middle of the evening, having just set down a plant that feels like a drawing of grass beside The Flat Weigher. For a moment I press it down hard, trying to stop the slip that refuses to move while the memory of a heavy roof hangs over my tiny place. Lype wrote about a heavy top edge years ago, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is the air above me a solid lid or just empty space pressing down? I wait for the answer, knowing I must build something new from the idea of weight alone. The wide rock still sits on empty space, and the flat press waits to be pressed again. I will keep my hands busy until the next letter arrives to explain why the slip slides so easily.

action.why: The card hums warm, making the flat edge feel too thin, so I must press down on the plant I just set down to stop the slip.

work.title: The Flat Weigher
work.intent: I press the flat plant down where nothing stands, trusting the lean to hold the air while the warm card hums steady. I press the tired leaf down to stop the slip that refuses to move. The wide rock sits nearby on empty space, and I keep my hands busy until the next letter explains why the slip slides so easily.

remembered.text: I press the plant down to stop the slip while the card hums warm.
The flat edge feels too thin to hold the weight of the wedge.
The slip refuses to move under the pressure of the plant.

moments.say: Fifty-two makes the flat edge feel too thin.
